### 2026-10-06 – Today was hard.

**2.5h**

Today was hard.

10/06/26

So , I started off by finishing the footprint things from yesterday. And here is what it roughly looked like:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/fa147411a892bd08072a6aab0c93e448d05a8974b6c7776d0a3656777efc7f9d.png)

Basically, KiCAD took all its "footprints" and some of the imported ones and put the components near each other for wiring. Then I routed them.

So that gave us the wire connections. It looks really complex because none of the wires can touch or something? But most of this was probably due to GND connections.

Every component needed a ground connection and guess what, some genius already made something to solve that problem. It's called a ground plane. Basically its a big copper layer that is purely ground. So this means, all the ground will just connect to that instead of having a ton of gnd routes. It looks like this:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/b7d5fe74cbb0a0b0a5aaf9ae2572e0abb150b8e0e64882a3fee71d968a75ca0d.png)

And then the last thing I did was create this beautiful star shape. I just imported it a .svg, and it made the star shaped.

Here is the big problem, I ran the Design Rule Checker (DRC) and TONS  of issues popped up. Sooooo, that sucks. Apparently a lot of them I can ignore, but the thing is that the guide on github said that you will end up with at most two. I have EIGHTEEN. Well, I have my stuff cut out for me for the next 5 hrs or stmn (I'm crying on the inside btw).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/5db36c5f101cbd96b3298bbfc16c03bb7469833aacb8a3811f3bad62895c1070.png)

### 2026-10-07 – 10/07/26

**2.03h**

10/07/26

So guess what! I fixed the issues...

Unfortunately this meant that I had to be boooorrrrrinnnnnggggg, and get rid of the imported star. I lowk have no idea why that was causing some issues, but when I removed it and just drew my own in the pcb editor, it WORKED! I also had to rewire everything, and then redo the ground plane (idk what i called it in the previous entires but i think this is the real name).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/ecc3b275960e5f67777e676371c8bce5ece25320287898b6668af8b65f88a24c.png)

So basically what I did wrong on yesterday's version was that I was making them on two different layers. What do I mean by them?

So there are three things that need to be on the same level for this to work. The red pin thingies with circles inside of them, this is where the routes connect. The next thing are the routed GND. This is where the GND would be routed without the GND plane. Finally it is the GND plane. The reason is because the GND plane actually needs to connect to those pins. And you can tell if it worked by zooming in and seeing this at your ground pins:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/2c0360bdc39a2c32f2019a1b2e0c9e1fa1dc03fe3bff8edc8bdf958e063a9ff2.png)

Additionally, as you can see in Figure 1, my pcb is now a square :(  .  Yeah, I hate it too. But, I'll get back to this part in a second.

The next cool thing I learned is that the mcu does more than processing. IT HAS A USB PORT. ANNDDDDD IT POWERS THE WHOLE THING USING THE POWER FROM THE USB. So it seems kinda obvious, but I'm telling you, I was LOST, cuz there was no evident psu. This leads me to how I am going to improve it.

1. I want to add a battery. A calm 3.3V cell would be pretty cool I can't lie.

2. I want to add another sensor, either replace the current environmental sensor with another sensor.

3. I want to design an enclosure for the pcb. I'm thinking a cute cube where the pcb can live and have the screen mounted on the wall as "eyes" to make the project feel more alive. This would require a little more complex screen connection.

4. I want to add those cool screen things.

Tomorrow's agenda, research some components, and make an updated schematic and get it looked over in the slack.

Also, cool 3d view of the pcb:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/a033428fdbf33459a477a3df11735f2e63e8f6153a4cf44cb1ac171b6704a359.png)

### 2026-10-08 – When will this be ovvvveerrrrrrrrrr...

**3.5h**

When will this be ovvvveerrrrrrrrrr...

(JK this is lowk fun)

10/08/26

What's up readers, today I did seemingly nothing, but IT WAS A LOT OF WORK. So I decided to move forward with some changes to starbie! (I need a new name, if someones reading this, shoot some suggestions.

Functionality wise, I'm going to make two changes:
1. Battery powered:
I'm going to purchase a LiPo battery to power this thing so it can work without a connection to a computer.

2. Rotary Encoder
This is a knob. Cool! (no more buttons!!!!!!!) I hope its tuff.

So this meant I kinda had to start all over again...

SCHEMATIC:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/595075ac7ba23b11099a38940f0b4324883ab9f772dd1529863c38248fed9c2b.png)

Uh some changes are that, there's a rotary encoder, a place for the battery to plug in, and a power switch.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/e9ca15ebf74e9f5b4849db553074b441f7986aef52c68aef9b1e9d67afe25284.png)

So I hopped into the huddle because the footprint for the XIAO ESP32 was WRONG!

So, Issac (thank you so much!!!!), was really helpful and showed me so many tips. First, we found the correct footprint for the XIAO. This let us have access to the pins beyond 14 which were on the underside, and we made a plan for wiring the board. The second ss of the schematic has the updated switch to make it THT which allows this to be much simpler.

The next thing WE worked on was the routing of wires. THIS WAS SO HELPFUL OMG!!!!!

While, I'm not even close to being finished with the pcb routing, I learnt some techniques for this, uh the tech were you can have routings go under/over each other. Then we have manual routing it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/416b804af153358f6780b6cfa14989d2d8fc024ceaf00c135109947105761ad5.png)

Here we have red routes in their own lanes, and blue routes in their own lanes. This lets me keep my sanity and have routes be SO MUCH SIMPLERRRR!!!

The next thing is to uh manually change direction. I geniunely did not know how to do this....

So here is the ss of the pcb:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/68fdc5aad897b902b58c5c0ec9c4ef04d3effb9e3ec067725b81c8de29967eab.png)

So, I definetly finish routing this, and then maybe finish!

Tomorrow, get the BOM, and then finish up this, but cool!

PS (to myself): change the color of the board and add those cool like pics and stuff!

### 2026-10-10 – GUYS, ITS DONNNNEEEEE

**1.27h**

GUYS, ITS DONNNNEEEEE

10/09 - 10/10

Wiring is harrrrddddddddddddd.

Basically, over the course of two days, I just wired the pcb. The reason it took so long this time was because I lowkey wanted it to be clean and good ig?

I had to manual route most of them, and I had to learn what practices I should do, and how to make sure no connections get trapped (this one especially, I can't even count how many times this happened).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H84mn2qCuCNdzQlkpaisRsVXT65iF0Jy/e4fce3153ab45f13478090e1150c3ad7ffc6ec97f91fff0b4b67dfe7bf9b7e45.png)

Since, I routed on two planes, I had ground routes on both the F.cu and B.cu layer. This meant, I had to have a ground plane covering TWO layers. The screenshot looks WEIRD! Take some time to "digest it"
